reauth_confirm.title: Repair AGL sign-in
reauth_confirm.description:
Home Assistant can no longer use this entry's AGL sign-in: AGL rejected the stored token (it expired or was revoked), AGL rejected a freshly refreshed one, or a rotated token could not be saved. Logging in again repairs the entry; your energy history is kept.

This keeps the certificate fingerprints already pinned for this entry. If Haggle reported that an AGL certificate changed, use **Reconfigure** from the entry's menu instead -- that is the step that re-pins.

Open the URL below in your browser and log in with the AGL login that owns this entry's contract. After login you will see a 'Not Found' page -- copy the full URL from the address bar and paste it in the field below.

`{authorize_url}`

data.callback_url: Callback URL (from address bar after login)

reconfigure.title: Re-pin AGL certificates
reconfigure.description:
Use this after Haggle reports that an AGL certificate changed. Logging in again refreshes this entry's AGL sign-in and re-captures the certificate fingerprints your Home Assistant host sees for secure.agl.com.au and api.platform.agl.com.au.

**Only continue on a network you trust.** Re-pinning trusts whatever certificate reaches your Home Assistant host right now. If anything between Home Assistant and AGL is intercepting TLS (a corporate proxy, a security appliance or an attacker), its certificate becomes the trusted one and the warning stops.

Open the URL below in your browser and log in with the AGL login that owns this entry's contract. After login you will see a 'Not Found' page -- copy the full URL from the address bar and paste it in the field below.

`{authorize_url}`

data.callback_url: Callback URL (from address bar after login)

select_contract.title: Choose AGL contract
select_contract.description: Select the electricity contract to monitor. If an error is shown, submit to try again.

error.invalid_auth: Login failed or callback URL is invalid. Try opening the authorize URL again.
error.cannot_connect: Could not reach AGL. Check your internet connection.

abort.already_configured: This AGL contract is already configured.
abort.no_electricity_contract: No electricity contract found on this AGL account. Haggle reads AGL's smart-meter electricity data; gas contracts are not supported.
abort.reconfigure_successful: AGL sign-in refreshed and certificate fingerprints re-pinned. Haggle is reloading.
abort.reconfigure_pin_incomplete: AGL sign-in refreshed, but the certificate could not be captured for one or both AGL hosts. The stored fingerprint for that host was kept and its warning remains. Haggle is reloading -- try Reconfigure again to finish re-pinning.
abort.contract_not_found: The AGL login you used does not include the contract this entry monitors (or that contract now belongs to a different AGL account). Nothing was changed. Log in with the AGL login that owns it; if the contract has closed or moved, remove this entry and add the integration again -- your existing statistics are kept. If Home Assistant had asked you to re-authenticate, reload the entry to see that prompt again.
abort.entry_not_repairable: This entry was created without a contract number and cannot be repaired in place. Remove it and add the integration again -- your existing statistics are kept.
abort.no_contracts: No contracts were found on this AGL account, so there is nothing for Haggle to read. Check that this is the AGL login that owns your electricity account, then try again.

solar_heal_gave_up.title: Solar history backfill gave up
solar_heal_gave_up.description: For entry {entry}: Haggle tried {attempts} times to backfill older solar history (back to {floor}), but AGL kept returning errors for at least one day, and has stopped retrying. The days that could not be fetched are permanently missing from the solar statistics. If those days matter to you, check whether the AGL app shows data for the same dates, then see the diagnostics guide (Learn more) for recovery options.

solar_repair_gave_up.title: Solar statistics repair gave up
solar_repair_gave_up.description: For entry {entry}: Haggle detected a downward step in the cumulative solar statistics and tried {attempts} times to rebuild the series (back to {floor}), but could not complete a clean sweep. A downward step may persist in the solar statistics. It can be corrected manually via Developer Tools → Statistics — see the diagnostics guide (Learn more).

solar_stall_gave_up.title: Solar backfill skipped {start} to {end}
solar_stall_gave_up.description: For entry {entry}: AGL returned errors for every day in {start}..{end} for {cycles} consecutive polls, so Haggle marked the span as covered and moved on. These days are recorded as zero export and will not be retried automatically — a permanent gap in the solar statistics. If the AGL app shows data for these dates, see the diagnostics guide (Learn more) for recovery options.

tz_realign_gave_up.title: Timezone history re-alignment stopped
tz_realign_gave_up.description: For entry {entry}: AGL's timestamps put South Australian and Broken Hill readings 30 minutes early, and Queensland readings 1 hour early while New South Wales is on daylight saving. Haggle tried to re-fetch the {stages} history from {floor} onward once to move it to the correct hours, but AGL kept returning errors or rate limits ({sweeps} failed attempts), so Haggle has stopped retrying. That history keeps the old timing: around midnight, the first part of a day can show at the end of the day before. Nothing is missing, but where the corrected recent week meets the older readings, one reading (30 minutes in South Australia and Broken Hill, 1 hour in Queensland) stays counted twice, so the running total is high by that one reading. New readings are still stored at the correct hours. Do not delete the haggle:* statistics to force a rebuild: Haggle only backfills the most recent 30 days, so anything older would be lost for good.

tz_history_before_realign.title: Older statistics keep their old timestamps
tz_history_before_realign.description: For entry {entry}: AGL's timestamps put South Australian and Broken Hill readings 30 minutes early, and Queensland readings 1 hour early while New South Wales is on daylight saving. Statistics from {floor} onward are at the correct hours (except solar statistics, if solar statistics writing is turned off in the options). Statistics stored before {floor} by a Haggle version older than 0.5.0-beta.3 may keep the old timing: around midnight, the first part of a day can show at the end of the day before, but nothing is missing or counted twice. If this entry was set up with 0.5.0-beta.3 or later, its history was never affected and you can dismiss this notice. Do not delete the haggle:* statistics to force a rebuild: Haggle only backfills the most recent 30 days, so anything older would be lost for good.

tariff_bands_legacy.title: Tariff bands follow AGL's unreliable tag
tariff_bands_legacy.description: For entry {entry}: Haggle writes your per-band statistics (Peak, Off-Peak, Shoulder, Anytime) by following the tariff tag AGL attaches to each half-hour reading. That tag often does not match your plan: peak-rate usage can show as Anytime, and a flat-rate plan can show a spurious Peak band. Your totals are still correct; only the split between bands is affected. To fix the split, open the integration's options, choose Tariff windows and enter your plan's time windows. If you do nothing, Haggle keeps the current behaviour for now, but this will change in a future release. See Learn more for which statistics to add to the Energy dashboard.

tariff_bands_invalid.title: Tariff window settings could not be read
tariff_bands_invalid.description: For entry {entry}: the stored tariff window settings are not valid (they may have been edited by hand or saved by a newer Haggle version), so Haggle is writing only the total consumption and cost statistics, with no per-band statistics. Open the integration's options, choose Tariff windows and save your windows again to fix this.

tariff_bands_suspended.title: Tariff bands paused: contract timezone unknown
tariff_bands_suspended.description: For entry {entry}: tariff windows are configured, but Haggle could not work out your contract's timezone from its service address, so it cannot tell which local half-hour each reading belongs to. Rather than put readings in the wrong band, Haggle is writing only the total consumption and cost statistics until the timezone is known. Per-band statistics for this period will be missing. If this notice persists, please open an issue and attach the integration's diagnostics file.

data_description.solar_statistics_enabled: Turn off to freeze all solar statistics writes (backfill, self-heal, give-up markers) without uninstalling or downgrading. Existing statistics are untouched; the bill-period solar sensors read 'unknown' while disabled and the cumulative sensors keep their last stored values. Takes effect from the next poll. Consumption statistics are unaffected.
data_description.poll_interval_hours: How often to check AGL for new data. AGL's own feed lags 24-48h behind real-time, so anything below 24h has nothing new to find -- the integration enforces a 24h floor. Raise this if you want to reduce request volume. Takes effect from the next poll.

tariff_windows.title: Tariff windows
tariff_windows.description: Enter the times of day your plan charges each rate, as on your bill. Times are local wall-clock time in half-hour steps, for example 15:00-21:00. Separate several windows with commas, and add weekdays or weekends after a window that applies only on those days (for example 07:00-09:00 weekdays). A window may wrap past midnight (22:00-07:00). Any time not covered by a window counts as the fallback band. Public holidays count as ordinary days. Changes take effect from the next scheduled poll; statistics from before then keep their previous split.

data_description.mode: Not configured keeps the current behaviour (bands follow AGL's own tag). Flat rate stops writing per-band statistics. Time-of-use windows assigns each half-hour to a band from its local time.
data_description.residual: Choose Anytime for plans with one general rate plus cheaper windows (for example EV plans), or Off-Peak for peak/shoulder/off-peak plans.
data_description.superoffpeak: For EV charging windows, or the free window of Victoria's Midday Power Saver tariff. Use Shoulder for its solar soak window.

rates.name: Rates (optional)
rates.description: Your plan's rate for each band, in cents per kWh including GST (between 1 and 500), as printed on your bill. These only feed the rate sensors; cost statistics always use AGL's own amounts. Takes effect from the next scheduled poll.

error.invalid_window_format: Use the format HH:MM-HH:MM, optionally followed by weekdays or weekends, with commas between windows.
error.window_not_half_hour: Windows must start and end on the hour or half-hour (:00 or :30).
error.window_empty: A window cannot start and end at the same time.
error.windows_overlap: Two windows overlap ({band_a} and {band_b}) on the same days. Each half-hour can belong to only one band.
error.no_windows: Enter at least one window, or choose Flat rate.
error.rate_out_of_range: Rates must be between 1 and 500 cents per kWh.
error.invalid_config: These settings could not be read. Please re-enter them.
error.unsupported_version: These settings were saved by a different Haggle version. Please re-enter them.
